idh.reasoning: For IDH status considered independently, the strongest MRI-demographic pattern favors IDH-mutant diffuse glioma: the patient is very young, the lesion has cortical involvement in a parietal/occipital cortical location, is solitary, and has no enhancing component on the provided post-contrast metadata. These features are more typical of an IDH-mutant lower-grade diffuse glioma than a conventional IDH-wildtype glioblastoma. Features arguing the other way are the very large tumor volume/size, deep white matter and ependymal involvement, midline shift, and the reported high necrosis proportion, which can be associated with more aggressive IDH-wildtype biology. However, the complete absence of enhancement makes typical IDH-wildtype glioblastoma less favored. Overall, the balance supports IDH-mutant status.

overall_comment: Predictions are based only on structured MRI metadata. The absence of enhancement strongly supports a lower-grade-appearing diffuse glioma, but the large size, mass effect, ependymal/deep white matter involvement, and reported necrosis proportion introduce uncertainty. Missing diffusion, perfusion, spectroscopy, and susceptibility/calcification information limit molecular subtyping, especially for 1p/19q status.

who_grade.reasoning: For CNS WHO grade considered independently, the imaging phenotype most strongly supports grade 2: the lesion is nonenhancing, has zero enhancing tumor volume, zero enhancing proportion, is solitary, and does not cross the midline. These are typical lower-grade imaging features. Against grade 2, the tumor is very large, produces midline shift and ventricular effacement, shows deep white matter and ependymal involvement, has measurable edema, and has a high reported necrosis proportion, all of which raise concern for higher grade. Still, in the provided metadata the absence of any enhancement is the most grade-discriminating feature and argues against a definite grade 3 or 4 imaging call. Overall, grade 2 is favored, with only modest confidence because of the aggressive mass-effect and invasion features.
